.github/workflows/checks.yml: The Windows client's Rust core and its conformance test against the real Node relay; later the shared wire fixtures and the plugin Hub too.
The help MCP bundle is generated from these (not CHANGELOG.md: the release PR changes only that).
The relay's tests also run the plugin's direct path end to end (src/direct.test.ts).
The website's Worker serves the help MCP server, so its tests run for both.
.github/workflows/paios-example.yml: --force and -f may be named only on a line that says they are not supported. The exemption is per line: "not supported" must appear on the same line as the flag.

Nothing but PAIOS/ (and this step's out.txt) appears in the folder, and the install holds no hidden file or folder, so no app-settings folder was created anywhere. Portable: macos find has no -printf. Count top-level entries without ls.
Option tokens: -x or --word at the start of a word.
PAIOS_ROOT wins when both are set.
The checks above leave the install as it was.
The installer and the self-test leave nothing behind in the temp folder.
Wiki-style [[links]] and query blocks need a particular app; only the optional guides under docs/ may show them.
curl's and bash's own flags in the one-liner are not installer flags.
.github/workflows/windows-installer.yml: app.ps1 expects the built app to carry it
